info.name: TAVLA API
info.description:
Enterprise Restaurant Reservation Platform — REST API (v1).

**Source of truth**: NestJS controllers under `apps/backend/src`, verified route-for-route by `scripts/verify-postman-coverage.ts` (AST-based, CI-suitable — see `npm run postman:verify`).

**Base URL**: `{{baseUrl}}` → `…/api/v1`

**Response envelope** (business endpoints unless noted):
```json
{ "success": true, "message": "...", "data": {}, "meta": {} }
```

**Structure**: four top-level business domains — `00 - System`, `01 - Customer`, `02 - Restaurant`, `03 - Platform Owner` — each subdivided by capability. An endpoint reachable by more than one actor type (e.g. a Customer or a branch-scoped Employee) is placed once, under its primary/canonical owner, with every supported actor documented in the request description rather than duplicated.

**Auth**: Collection Bearer defaults to `{{accessToken}}` (Restaurant Owner/Admin/Employee). Public requests set `noauth` explicitly. Every request under `01 - Customer` uses `{{customerAccessToken}}` explicitly; every request under `03 - Platform Owner` uses `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}` explicitly.

**Role labels** are documented on every request under **Required Role**.

Each backend route appears **exactly once** — verified 100% coverage, zero missing/extra/duplicate routes.

## Purpose
Request deletion of the authenticated Customer's own account
## Authorization
Bearer `{{customerAccessToken}}`.
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard
## Required Role
Customer only - never reachable by Employee/OrganizationMember/PlatformAdmin actors, even though they are also User rows underneath.
## Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- `Content-Type: application/json`
## Path Params
_None_
## Query Params
_None_
## Body
JSON body — DTO: `DeleteAccountRequestDto`
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Account deletion requested. You have until the grace period ends to cancel."
Body: `DeleteAccountResponseDto` — `scheduledAnonymizationAt` (ISO 8601).
## Behavior (ADR-014)
- Anonymization-in-place, never immediate physical deletion.
- Immediately revokes every DeviceSession/TokenFamily and bumps `sessionVersion` — every already-issued access token on every device is rejected on its very next request, not just on refresh.
- Auto-cancels any active waitlist entries.
- Rejected with 409 while any Pending/Approved reservation exists — cancel it first via the existing reservation cancellation flow, then retry.
- Irreversible anonymization executes automatically once `SystemConfiguration.anonymizationGracePeriodDays` (default 30) elapses, unless cancelled first via `POST /users/me/cancel-deletion`.
- Idempotent: repeating this call while a request is already pending re-verifies the password (so a stale/malicious caller can't probe schedule state without credentials) but does not reschedule, re-publish the event, or write a duplicate audit row.
## Error Responses
- **400**: VALIDATION_ERROR (missing/too-short password)
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN, AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS (wrong password)
- **403**: AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED, AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, AUTH_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, FORBIDDEN (actor is not a Customer)
- **409**: OPEN_RESERVATIONS_BLOCK_DELETION
## Notes
- Controller: `UsersController`.`deleteCurrentAccount`
- Full path: `/api/v1/users/me`
- Callers: Customer only (actor-type gate enforced in the use case)

## Purpose
Cancel a pending account deletion request within the grace period
## Authorization
Bearer `{{customerAccessToken}}`.
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard
## Required Role
Customer
## Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
## Path Params
_None_
## Query Params
_None_
## Body
_None_ — no password required. A freshly-issued JWT (obtained by logging back in, since requesting deletion already revoked every prior session) is already proof of credential possession.
## Success Response
204 No Content (envelope skipped).
## Behavior
Idempotent: calling this with no pending deletion request is a silent success (still 204).
## Error Responses
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN
- **403**: FORBIDDEN (actor is not a Customer)
## Notes
- Controller: `UsersController`.`cancelCurrentAccountDeletion`
- Full path: `/api/v1/users/me/cancel-deletion`
- Callers: Customer only (actor-type gate enforced in the use case)

## Purpose
Export the authenticated user's own data (GDPR right to portability)
## Authorization
Bearer `{{customerAccessToken}}`.
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard
## Required Role
Customer
## Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
## Path Params

## Query Params
_None_
## Body
_None_
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Data export generated successfully."
Body: `ExportUserDataResponseDto` — `exportedAt`, `profile`, `preferences`, `reservations` (`{items, total}`), `reviews` (`{items, total}`), `favorites` (`{items, total}`).
## Behavior (ADR-014 §5)
Offered before/during the account deletion flow, never only after. Aggregates Profile, Preferences, Reservations, Reviews, and Favorites via the same use cases their own dedicated endpoints already use — MVP scope, capped at 1000 records per category.
## Error Responses
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN
- **403**: AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED, AUTH_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, AUTH_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED
## Notes

## Purpose
Returns the authenticated Customer's complete reservation set (upcoming + history combined), enriched with Restaurant/Branch/Table display fields (one joined query, no N+1).
## Authorization
Bearer `{{customerAccessToken}}`.
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard
## Required Role
Customer (User actor only - an Employee or OrganizationMember token is rejected with 403, even if it happens to own the reservation)
## Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
## Path Params
_None_
## Query Params
- `page`, `limit` - pagination
- `restaurantId`, `branchId` - filter by restaurant/branch
- `dateFrom`, `dateTo` - inclusive reservationDate range
- `sort` (reservationDate | createdAt), `order` (asc | desc)
- `status` - the only one of the four GET /reservations/my* routes that accepts this filter
## Body
_None_
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Your reservations retrieved successfully."
## Error Responses
- **400**: VALIDATION_ERROR (invalid page/limit/status/date/sort/order)
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN
- **403**: FORBIDDEN (caller is not a Customer)
## Notes
- Controller: `ReservationsController.myReservations`
- Full path: `/api/v1/reservations/my`
- Always resolves from the caller's own JWT userId, never a client-supplied id.

## Purpose
Get one of the authenticated Customer's own reservations by id - the complete flat Reservation shape (all Reservation aggregate fields), reusing the existing reservation response mapper (toReservationResponse) - not the enriched restaurant/branch/table projection the other three GET /reservations/my* routes return.
## Authorization

Customer (User actor only - an Employee or OrganizationMember token is rejected with 403, even if it happens to own the reservation)
## Headers
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
## Path Params

## Query Params
_None_
## Body
_None_

Envelope message: "Reservation retrieved successfully."

- **400**: VALIDATION_ERROR (reservationId is not a valid UUID)
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN
- **403**: FORBIDDEN (caller is not a Customer)

- Controller: `ReservationsController.myReservationDetails`

request.description:
## Purpose
Restaurant Dashboard Calendar. Returns a branch's reservations within a required, bounded `[dateFrom, dateTo]` date range (inclusive, against `reservationDate`), enriched with Table and Customer (User/Guest) display fields - one joined query, no N+1, served entirely by the existing `(branchId, reservationDate, status)` index. Ordered `reservationStartTime` ascending.

One endpoint serves all three calendar views - pick `dateFrom`/`dateTo` accordingly:
- **Day**: `dateFrom` = `dateTo` = the selected day, e.g. `dateFrom=2026-08-15&dateTo=2026-08-15`
- **Week**: `dateFrom` = week start, `dateTo` = week end, e.g. `dateFrom=2026-08-10&dateTo=2026-08-16`
- **Month**: `dateFrom` = month start, `dateTo` = month end, e.g. `dateFrom=2026-08-01&dateTo=2026-08-31`
## Authorization
Bearer `{{accessToken}}` (Employee actor).
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard (no PermissionsGuard - this is a read, not a `reservations:*` mutation; see Notes).
## Required Role
Employee only, branch-scoped (empty `branchIds` on the JWT = restaurant-wide scope). A Customer or OrganizationMember actor is rejected with 403 - OrganizationMember has no direct REST read access to the Reservation resource in this API (mirrors every other `/reservations/*` route's own actor-type rule).
## Path Params
| Name | Variable | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| `restaurantId` | `{{restaurantId}}` | UUID path parameter |
| `branchId` | `{{branchId}}` | UUID path parameter |
## Query Params
- `dateFrom`, `dateTo` - REQUIRED, inclusive `reservationDate` range (max span 366 days)
- `status` - optional single-status filter
- `page`, `limit` - pagination
## Body
_None_
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Branch reservations retrieved successfully."
## Error Responses
- **400**: VALIDATION_ERROR (missing/invalid dateFrom/dateTo, dateFrom after dateTo, range exceeds 366 days, invalid page/limit)
- **401**: AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, AUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN
- **403**: FORBIDDEN (not an Employee), EMPLOYEE_BRANCH_NOT_ASSIGNED (Employee not assigned to this branch)
- **404**: NOT_FOUND (restaurant not found, or branch not found / belongs to another restaurant - IDOR-safe collapse)
## Notes
- Controller: `BranchReservationsController.list`
- Full path: `/api/v1/restaurants/:restaurantId/branches/:branchId/reservations`
- No new `reservations:*` permission was introduced for this route (TASKS.md Phase 8 §9: existing mutation permissions remain REST-command-only) - any branch-authorized Employee may read the calendar.
- Audit-driven addition (2026-08-10): a full repository audit found no existing restaurant-dashboard reservation list/calendar endpoint - every prior `GET /reservations*` route is Customer-ownership-scoped. This single date-range endpoint was added instead of three redundant `/calendar/day|week|month` routes.

response.name: 200 OK - day view
401 Unauthorized - missing/expired access token
403 Forbidden - actor is not an Employee
403 Forbidden - Employee not assigned to this branch
404 Not Found - branch not found (or belongs to another restaurant)
400 Bad Request - dateFrom after dateTo

## Purpose
Restaurant Dashboard: broadcast an internal in-app notification to all eligible Customers platform-wide (Phase 19.9, ADR-037).
## Authorization

Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard, OrganizationMemberGuard
## Required Role

## Path Params

JSON body - DTO: `SendNotificationBroadcastRequestDto`

## Error Responses
- 403 FORBIDDEN - caller is not an Owner/Admin organization member
- 404 NOT_FOUND - restaurantId does not exist or belongs to another Organization (IDOR-safe)
## Notes
- Audience is platform-wide (same eligibility as the Platform Admin broadcast) - restaurantId proves the caller controls this Restaurant and is recorded for audit, but never narrows the audience (explicit product decision).

Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard, OrganizationMemberGuard

Owner or Admin

- **403**: FORBIDDEN

## Notes

- Full path: `/api/v1/organizations/invitations`

## Purpose

Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard, OrganizationMemberGuard

Owner or Admin
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Invitations retrieved successfully."
## Notes
- Controller: `OrganizationInvitationsController`.`list`
- Full path: `/api/v1/organizations/invitations`

## Purpose

## Authorization
Bearer `{{accessToken}}`.
Guards: JwtAuthGuard, SessionVersionGuard, OrganizationMemberGuard
## Required Role
Owner or Admin
## Path Params
- `invitationId` (uuid)
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Invitation revoked successfully."
## Error Responses
- **403**: FORBIDDEN
- **404**: NOT_FOUND
- **409**: CONFLICT (no longer pending)
## Notes
- Controller: `OrganizationInvitationsController`.`revoke`
- Full path: `/api/v1/organizations/invitations/:invitationId`

## Purpose
Accept an Organization invitation (Phase 19.8, ADR-036). PUBLIC route - not session-guarded, security rests entirely on the opaque token from the emailed link.
If the invited email already has an account, send a Bearer token for that exact account (firstName/lastName/password are ignored) - 401 if anonymous, 403 if a different account.
If the invited email has no account yet, firstName/lastName/password are required and a new account is created atomically with the membership. The invited email itself always comes from the token, never the request body.
## Authorization
None required (public route). Optional Bearer `{{accessToken}}` for the existing-account branch.
## Path Params
- `token` (opaque invitation token from the emailed link)
## Body (new-account branch only)
`{ "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Doe", "password": "BrandNewPassw0rd!" }`
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Invitation accepted successfully."
## Error Responses
- **400**: INVALID_INVITATION_TOKEN / EXPIRED_INVITATION_TOKEN
- **401**: UNAUTHORIZED (invited email already has an account - log in first)
- **403**: FORBIDDEN (authenticated as a different account)
- **409**: CONFLICT (Organization no longer available, already an active member, or lost a concurrent-accept race)
## Notes
- Controller: `OrganizationInvitationAcceptanceController`.`accept`
- Full path: `/api/v1/invitations/:token/accept`

item.name: 03 - Platform Owner

request.description:
## Purpose
Authenticate as Platform Admin and open a console session.

Issues a short-lived access token signed with the isolated Platform Admin
secret/issuer/audience, **and** an opaque refresh token backed by a
`PlatformAdminSession` row. The refresh token is what `POST /platform-admin/refresh`
rotates and `POST /platform-admin/logout` revokes.
## Authorization
None (public — this IS the authentication step).
## Body
JSON — DTO: `PlatformAdminLoginRequestDto` (`email`, `password`)
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Login successful."
## Error Responses
- **401** `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — unknown email, wrong password, or not an active
  Platform Admin. All three are deliberately indistinguishable.
  **Password-strength rules are NOT applied here** — a short or simple wrong password
  still returns 401, never a 400 validation error.
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminController`.`login`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/login`
- The refresh token is shown exactly once; only its SHA-256 digest is stored.

request.description:
## Purpose
Rotate the refresh token and obtain a new access token.
## Authorization
None — the refresh token in the body IS the credential (same model as `POST /auth/refresh`).
## Body
JSON — DTO: `PlatformAdminRefreshRequestDto` (`refreshToken`)
## Behavior
- The presented token is consumed; a brand-new pair is returned.
- Replaying an already-rotated token is treated as theft: **every** session
  belonging to that admin is revoked and the attempt is audited.
- Unknown, expired, revoked and replayed tokens are indistinguishable in the response.
- The admin `PlatformAdmin` row is re-read, so a revoked admin cannot refresh.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Session refreshed successfully." — same shape as login.
## Error Responses
- **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` — missing/empty `refreshToken`
- **401** `AUTH_INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN`
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminController`.`refresh`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/refresh`

request.description:
## Purpose
End one Platform Owner console session.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard
## Body
JSON — DTO: `PlatformAdminLogoutRequestDto` (`refreshToken`)

The refresh token is required because Platform Admin access tokens carry no
`sessionId` claim (AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md §5.2 keeps those claims minimal).
## Behavior
- Revokes the `PlatformAdminSession`, so the refresh token stops working immediately.
- The already-issued **access token stays valid until it expires** (900s default) —
  inherent to stateless JWT verification, identical to `POST /auth/logout`.
- Idempotent and non-enumerating: unknown, already-revoked, or another admin’s token
  all return 204.
## Success Response
**204 No Content** — no body.
## Error Responses
- **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR`
- **401** `UNAUTHORIZED` — missing/malformed/expired access token
- **403** `FORBIDDEN` — caller is no longer an active Platform Admin
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminController`.`logout`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/logout`

request.description:
## Purpose
Identity and **live** role of the authenticated Platform Admin.

What a console calls on boot to answer "am I still signed in, and as whom?"
without decoding the JWT client-side or trusting cached login state.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard

Available to **both** Platform tiers — it reports the caller’s own role rather
than requiring a particular one.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Current Platform Admin retrieved successfully."

`role` is read from the live `PlatformAdmin` row, not echoed from the JWT claim,
so a demotion appears on the next call rather than at next login.
## Error Responses
- **401** `UNAUTHORIZED` — missing/malformed/expired access token (refresh, then retry)
- **403** `FORBIDDEN` — token valid but the admin grant was revoked (do not retry)
- **404** `NOT_FOUND` — grant or User row no longer exists
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminController`.`me`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/me`
- Never exposes the password hash or session/permissions versions.

## Purpose
Create a Restaurant inside a named Organization, directly from the Platform Owner console.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
**PlatformAdmin only** — this is a mutation, and PlatformSupport is read-only (ADR-034 §11).
## Body
JSON — DTO: `PlatformAdminCreateRestaurantRequestDto`
(`organizationId` + every field of `CreateRestaurantRequestDto`)
## Behavior
ADR-035 Pattern 1 — rebinds to the supplied `organizationId`, then reuses the ordinary
`CreateRestaurantUseCase`, so Restaurant + RestaurantSettings + RestaurantUsage are
created in one transaction exactly as on the Owner path.

**Subscription limits still apply.** A Platform Owner does not bypass the plan’s
`maxRestaurants` cap; exceeding it returns 409.
## Success Response
**201 Created**, message "Restaurant created successfully." — the same body shape as
`GET /platform-admin/restaurants/:id`, so the console can render the new Restaurant
without a follow-up call.
## Error Responses
- **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR`
- **401** `UNAUTHORIZED`
- **403** `FORBIDDEN` — caller is PlatformSupport, or not an active admin
- **404** `NOT_FOUND` — organization missing, soft-deleted, or has no Subscription
- **409** `CONFLICT` / `ORGANIZATION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminRestaurantsController`.`create`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/restaurants`

request.description:
## Purpose
Paginated listing / narrow lookup of Restaurants (ADR-034 §13 — a support tool, not a search engine).
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport (read-only endpoint)
## Query Params
- `q` (optional) — case-insensitive partial match on name or slug.
  **An empty or whitespace-only `q` returns the ordinary paginated list**, never an
  empty page: no filter clause is emitted at all (no `LIKE '%%'`).
- `status` (optional) — `Active` | `Suspended` | `Deleted`. `Active`/`Suspended` match the
  status column and exclude soft-deleted rows; `Deleted` matches soft-deleted rows
  regardless of status. Omitted returns every Restaurant, soft-deleted included.
- `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100)
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Restaurants retrieved successfully."
`data`: `{ items: [{ id, organizationId, name, slug, status, deletedAt }], total, page, limit }`

`total` is the full count matching the **same** filter as the returned page.
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminRestaurantsController`.`search`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/restaurants`
- Ordered newest first (`createdAt DESC`).

request.description:
## Purpose
Paginated listing / narrow lookup of Organizations (ADR-034 §13).
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport (read-only endpoint)
## Query Params
- `q` (optional) — case-insensitive partial match on name or slug.
  **An empty or whitespace-only `q` returns the ordinary paginated list**, never an empty page.
- `status` (optional) — `Active` | `Suspended` | `Deleted`. (`Closed` is deliberately not
  offered: ADR-034 §4/§5 records it as an unused value no PlatformAdmin action writes.)
- `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100)
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Organizations retrieved successfully."
`data`: `{ items: [{ id, name, slug, status, deletedAt }], total, page, limit }`
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminOrganizationsController`.`search`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/organizations`

request.description:
## Purpose
Full Organization detail by id, with live restaurant and active-member counts.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport (read-only endpoint)
## Path Params
- `id` (uuid) — the Organization id
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Organization retrieved successfully."

`restaurantCount` excludes soft-deleted restaurants; `memberCount` counts Active
members only (excludes Invited and Removed). Both are aggregated in the same query
as the record, so they cannot describe a different instant than it does.
## Behavior
A **soft-deleted Organization is returned** (with `deletedAt` set) rather than 404,
so the console can inspect one before deciding whether to Restore it.
## Error Responses
- **401** `UNAUTHORIZED`
- **403** `FORBIDDEN`
- **404** `NOT_FOUND`
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminOrganizationsController`.`getById`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/organizations/:id`

request.description:
## Purpose
Paginated, searchable listing of **every** account.

This is the endpoint that makes the four `/platform-admin/accounts/:userId/*` actions
usable: before it existed, a console had no way to *find* a `userId` and an operator
had to paste a UUID obtained from outside the API.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport (read-only endpoint)
## Query Params
- `q` (optional) — case-insensitive partial match across email, phone, username,
  firstName and lastName. **Empty or whitespace-only returns the ordinary paginated
  list**, never an empty page.
- `status` (optional) — a `UserStatus` value.
- `accountType` (optional) — `PlatformAdmin` | `OrganizationMember` | `Employee` | `Customer`.
  Derived from which relations the `User` row has, not a stored column; precedence is
  PlatformAdmin → OrganizationMember → Employee → Customer.
- `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100)
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Accounts retrieved successfully."
`data`: `{ items: [...], total, page, limit }` — `total` matches the same filter as the page.
## Security
Never exposes `passwordHash`, `sessionVersion` or `permissionsVersion`.
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminAccountAccessController`.`list`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/accounts`
- Ordered newest first (`createdAt DESC`).

request.description:
## Purpose
Full account detail by `userId`.

Carries the operational state needed to answer "why can this account not log in?"
in one call — `status`, `emailVerified`, `failedLoginCount`, `lockedUntil`,
`activeSessionCount`, the pending-deletion timestamps, and Organization memberships.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport (read-only endpoint)
## Path Params
- `userId` (uuid)
## Behavior
Soft-deleted and anonymized accounts are **returned** (with `deletedAt`/`anonymizedAt` set)
rather than 404 — seeing that an account was deleted is the point of looking it up.
Only a genuinely nonexistent id is a 404.

`activeSessionCount` is what Force Logout would terminate: device sessions that are
neither revoked nor expired right now.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Account retrieved successfully."
## Security
Never exposes `passwordHash`, `sessionVersion` or `permissionsVersion`.
## Error Responses
- **401** `UNAUTHORIZED`
- **403** `FORBIDDEN`
- **404** `NOT_FOUND`
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminAccountAccessController`.`get`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/accounts/:userId`

in one call — `status`, `emailVerified`, `failedLoginCount`, `lockedUntil`,

request.description:
## Purpose
Notification broadcast history with **real** delivery state.

The counterpart to `POST /platform-admin/notifications/broadcast`, which returns
**202 Accepted** and therefore cannot report an outcome — delivery happens
asynchronously via BullMQ, minutes later. Without this endpoint a console has no way
to learn whether a broadcast actually went out.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`. Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin **or** PlatformSupport — read-only, even though *authoring* a broadcast
is PlatformAdmin-only.
## Query Params
- `status` (optional) — `Pending` | `Processing` | `Completed` | `Failed`
- `senderType` (optional) — `PlatformAdmin` | `OrganizationMember`. Omitted returns both;
  a Platform Owner auditing outbound messaging generally wants all of it.
- `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100)
## Field semantics (all persisted, none synthesized at read time)
- `status` — the aggregate’s own state machine: `Pending` (queued, fan-out not started)
  → `Processing` → `Completed` (audience exhausted) | `Failed` (terminal, after BullMQ
  retries were exhausted).
- `totalRecipients` — audience-size snapshot taken at queue time; `null` until resolved.
  Observability only: the live audience can shift before the fan-out runs.
- `processedCount` — advances by the full batch size per processed batch.
- `succeededCount` — notification rows actually inserted.
- `failedCount` — rows skipped as already-delivered on a retried batch. **Not an error
  count** — a resumed broadcast legitimately re-covers recipients it already reached.
- `updatedAt` — last counter/status write, i.e. when delivery last progressed.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Notification broadcasts retrieved successfully."
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminNotificationsController`.`listBroadcasts`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/notifications`
- Ordered newest first (`createdAt DESC`).

request.description:
## Purpose
Broadcast an internal in-app notification to all eligible Customers platform-wide (Phase 19.9, ADR-037).
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}` (Platform Admin issuer).
Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin only
## Body
JSON body - DTO: `SendNotificationBroadcastRequestDto`
## Success Response
202 Accepted - `{ broadcastId, totalRecipients }`. Queued only - processed asynchronously in batches via BullMQ; 202 does not mean delivery has completed.
## Error Responses
- 403 FORBIDDEN - caller is not an active PlatformAdmin
## Notes
- Audience: every active Customer account (no OrganizationMember/Employee/PlatformAdmin row) with marketingOptIn enabled, platform-wide.
- Internal notification system only - no Firebase/OneSignal/FCM/APNs.

## Follow-up
**202 means queued, not delivered.** Poll `GET /platform-admin/notifications` for the real outcome — `status`, `processedCount`, `succeededCount`, `failedCount` are written asynchronously by the BullMQ fan-out processor.

Preview a proposed fee against recent acquisition volume for a Restaurant.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`.
Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin or PlatformSupport (read-only, both tiers)
## Body
JSON body — DTO: `SimulatePricingRequestDto`. `lookbackDays` optional, 1-365, default applies server-side.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Pricing simulation computed successfully." `data`: `SimulatePricingResponseDto` (`isEstimateOnly` always `true` — nothing is persisted)
## Error Responses
- **403**: FORBIDDEN
- **404**: RESTAURANT_NOT_FOUND
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminPricingController`.`simulate`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/pricing/simulate`
- Stateless (ADR-033 §19) — never a commitment.

request.description:
## Purpose
Revenue report over CustomerAcquisition, bucketed by the requested dimension.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`.
Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin or PlatformSupport (read-only, both tiers)
## Parameters
- `from`/`to` (required, ISO 8601)
- `groupBy` (required): `day`\|`week`\|`month`\|`quarter`\|`year`\|`restaurant`\|`organization`\|`source`
- `restaurantId`/`organizationId` (optional, UUID filters)
## Body
_None_
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Revenue report computed successfully." `data`: `{ groupBy, buckets: [{key,currency,recordedCount,recordedTotal,reversedCount,reversedTotal}] }`
## Error Responses
- **403**: FORBIDDEN
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminRevenueController`.`report`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/revenue/report`
- Recorded/Reversed metrics only (ADR-033 §22) — never Collected/Outstanding. Buckets are partitioned by currency, never summed (no FX conversion).

response.name: 200 — Monthly buckets, partitioned by currency

item.name: Platform Admin Accounts
item.description: Platform Admin / Platform Support account CRUD (ADR-034 §10-12). Reads are available to both Platform tiers; every mutation is PlatformAdmin-only, since PlatformSupport has no mutation authority (§11). There is no hard delete — Deactivate sets `revokedAt` and is the delete capability.

request.description:
## Purpose
Create a Platform Admin or Platform Support account.
## Authorization
Bearer `{{platformAdminAccessToken}}`.
Guards: PlatformAdminGuard, PlatformAdminRoleGuard
## Required Role
PlatformAdmin only
## Body
JSON body — DTO: `CreatePlatformAdminRequestDto`. `role` is `PlatformAdmin` or `PlatformSupport`.
## Success Response
Envelope message: "Platform Admin account created successfully." `data`: `PlatformAdminAccountResponseDto`
## Error Responses
- **403**: FORBIDDEN — PlatformSupport cannot mutate
- **409**: CONFLICT — email already exists
## Notes
- Controller: `PlatformAdminAccountsController`.`create`
- Full path: `/api/v1/platform-admin/admins`
- Mirrors Restaurant Owner provisioning's trust model — final password, no OTP step.

item.description: Owner provisioning and Organization subscription administration. Platform Admin *account* management lives in the sibling "Platform Admin Accounts" folder.

Platform Owner (Farid Dashboard) API surface.

**Authentication.** `POST /platform-admin/login` issues an access token *and* an opaque
refresh token backed by a `PlatformAdminSession` row. Rotate with
`POST /platform-admin/refresh`, end the session with `POST /platform-admin/logout`, and
check who you are with `GET /platform-admin/me`. This pipeline is fully isolated from the
tenant one: its own secret, issuer and audience — an ordinary Customer/Owner/Employee token
is rejected outright.

**401 vs 403.** `401 UNAUTHORIZED` means no usable credential (missing, malformed, expired,
wrong signature) — refresh, then retry. `403 FORBIDDEN` means the token is valid but the
caller lacks authority (revoked grant, or a PlatformSupport tier attempting a mutation) —
refreshing will not help.

**Search and pagination.** Every list endpoint takes `q`, `page` and `limit`; Restaurants,
Organizations and Accounts also take `status`. An empty or whitespace-only `q` returns the
ordinary paginated list, never an empty page. `total` always describes the same filter as
the returned page.

**Response envelope.** Success: `{ success: true, message, data, meta }`.
Error: `{ success: false, message, code, errors, timestamp, path }`.
